instruction: I have jotted down my amazon shopping list in simple_note. Reset my amazon cart to have as many products in as many quantities from this list as available, and tell me its total cost. In calculating the total cost (i) only include the available items, and (ii) include tax, but not delivery fees as I will be using prime later.
notes: The shopping-list note contents are unknown at planning time, so the problem uses placeholder list items (3 items: two purchasable in quantities 2 and 1, one unavailable); the real number of items, their ids and purchasable quantities are read at runtime from simple_note.show_note and amazon.show_product. Availability/purchasable quantity are static world facts in :init (like password-for) and become usable only after amazon.show_product asserts (availability-known); unavailable items are only checked, never added, since no (purchasable ...) fact exists for them. Cart reset is modeled as a separate amazon.clear_cart before the adds (clear_cart_first=True on the first add_product_to_cart is an equivalent alternative); clear-cart can run only once and all adds require (cart-cleared), so nothing is cleared after adding. (cart-cost-current) is deleted by every cart-changing action and re-asserted by amazon.show_cart, forcing the cost to be read after the final cart change; the answer is the cart total including tax but excluding delivery fee. supervisor-complete-task carries the generic goal conditions (cart-cleared, found-total-cost, cart-cost-current) and (not (task-completed)); the per-product in-cart / availability-known goal facts name problem objects and so are enforced in :goal, while (not (task-completed)) on every other action still guarantees complete_task is last.
